display.purpose: Admin stat-card figures only. One per tile, brass, 28px/700 — the loudest element on an admin screen.

data.purpose: Overview stat figures (nights, walking days, km, metres of ascent). 22px/800, colour-coded to meaning.

headline.purpose: Checklist owner name (18px/700) and admin section titles (16px/700).

title.purpose: The workhorse. Day routes, hut names, member names, list-item names, button labels. 13px/600.

body.purpose: Hebrew descriptions, notes, equipment item names. 13-14px/400, line-height 1.5. 14px is the document base.

label.purpose: Section headings, field labels, day numbers, status pills, role tags, wordmark. 10-11px/600, uppercase where Latin, 0.06-0.12em tracking, Stone Muted. The most characteristic type in the system.

shadows.name: over-map-float
shadows.purpose: Toast and MapLibre popups. Says 'this is above the terrain'.

shadows.name: marker-lift
shadows.purpose: Day-number bubbles and geocoder preview pins on the satellite map.

shadows.name: marker-drop
shadows.purpose: Hut markers — a filter, not a box-shadow, so it follows the marker's composite silhouette including its triangle tip.

shadows.name: floating-control
shadows.purpose: The mobile hamburger, which sits over live content.

shadows.name: scrim
shadows.purpose: Drawer occlusion layer. Not a shadow — it darkens what is behind, it does not lift what is in front.

motion.name: state-fast
motion.purpose: Default for every colour, border and opacity state change: buttons, chips, nav, rows, inputs, marker hover.

motion.name: surface-slow
motion.purpose: Drawers, overlays and the toast fade.

motion.name: ease-drawer
motion.purpose: The only named easing in the system; drawer slide only. Everything else uses the browser default.

motion.name: map-ease
motion.purpose: MapLibre camera moves: 600ms 3D pitch toggle, 800ms day-segment fly, 1000ms fly-to-hut, 1400ms fitBounds on a geocoded segment. Deliberately slower than UI motion because the terrain has to stay legible during the move.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one committing action per form — sign in, add, save.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #c9a84c; color: #000; font-weight: 600; font-size: 13px; letter-spacing: .04em; padding: 10px 18px; border: none; border-radius: 2px; cursor: pointer; transition: opacity .15s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { opacity: .85; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #c9a84c; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: .4; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: The default action shape. Transparent on a hairline; hover reveals brass without a fill.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { background: transparent; color: #6b6660; font-size: 12px; letter-spacing: .04em; padding: 7px 14px; border: 1px solid #272727; border-radius: 2px; cursor: pointer; transition: all .15s; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { border-color: rgba(201,168,76,.3); color: #c9a84c; } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #c9a84c; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Danger Button
components.description: Destructive action. Never a solid red fill — red text that fills with its own wash on hover.
components.css: .ds-btn-danger { background: transparent; color: #d95757; font-size: 12px; letter-spacing: .04em; padding: 7px 14px; border: 1px solid rgba(217,87,87,.12); border-radius: 2px; cursor: pointer; transition: all .15s; } .ds-btn-danger:hover { background: rgba(217,87,87,.12); border-color: #d95757; } .ds-btn-danger:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #c9a84c; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Filter Chip
components.description: Equipment-category and map-layer toggles. Selected and hover render identically so the control previews its own on-state.

components.name: Input Field
components.description: Recessed field with an engraved label above. Focus shifts the border to brass — no glow, no size change.

narrative.overview:
This is not an app that wants to be admired; it is a panel of instruments read in bad light by someone who is tired. The ground is near-black (#0c0c0c), surfaces step up in almost imperceptible increments of grey, and every division is a single 1px hairline. Corners are 2px — effectively square. Nothing glows, nothing gradients, nothing floats unless it is physically above the map. The one non-neutral colour, a muted brass, is used the way a machined bezel is used: to mark the live control and nothing else.

The reason the restraint works is the map. Behind and beside every panel sits a 3D satellite render of the Mont Blanc massif with eight saturated route lines drawn across it. The chrome has to recede or the terrain becomes unreadable. So the interface deliberately spends its colour budget on data — one bright hue per hiking day, three status hues for booked / pending / unbooked — and keeps the frame monochrome. Where the interface does raise its voice it is always about a fact: a 28px number, a status pill, an ⚠️ payment still owed at Rifugio Elisabetta.

The language is Hebrew and the direction is right-to-left, natively — labels, drawers, active-state bars and the route sidebar all begin at the right edge. Latin place names sit inside that RTL flow untranslated, and the wordmark is wide-tracked uppercase Latin. That collision — Hebrew task language around French and Italian mountain names — is the system's actual signature and should not be smoothed away.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black ground with three barely-separated surface steps; depth by tone, not shadow
2px corners everywhere; the interface reads as machined, not soft
One brass accent, reserved for live state; all other colour is data or status
Dense uppercase micro-labels (10-11px, 0.1em tracking) over full-size headings
System font stack only — no webfont, no display face
RTL-first: leading edge is the right edge
Colour saturation belongs to the map, not the chrome

rules.name: The Colour-Belongs-To-Data Rule
rules.body: If a saturated colour on screen is not (a) the brass on the one live control, (b) a booked/pending/unbooked status, or (c) a per-day route identity, it is wrong. Chrome is grey.

rules.name: The Two-Register Rule
rules.body: A status colour never appears as a bare tint. It appears as full-strength text or stroke on its own 12%-alpha wash, or not at all.

rules.name: The Warm-White Rule
rules.body: #e6e3dc in the interface; #fff only for marks drawn over the satellite map, where it is a casing colour against terrain.

rules.name: The Engraved-Label Rule
rules.body: Any label that names a region, field, state or unit is 10-11px, weight 600, uppercase where Latin, tracked 0.1em, in Stone Muted. Never sentence-case, never body weight.

rules.name: The Fixed-Scale Rule
rules.body: No clamp(), no vw type. Users read this at a consistent DPI on a phone or a laptop; a heading that shrinks inside a 240px sidebar looks broken, not responsive. Mobile raises specific sizes explicitly rather than fluidly.

rules.name: The Hebrew-Is-Not-Uppercased Rule
rules.body: text-transform: uppercase is a no-op on Hebrew and is applied for the Latin labels and the wordmark. Do not add tracking to Hebrew body copy in imitation of it.

rules.name: The Flat-Until-You-Float Rule
rules.body: A shadow is permitted only on an element physically above the map canvas or above the app shell. Cards, panels, tiles, list items, forms, drawers and buttons stay flat forever; they separate by tone and hairline. No hover lift, no translateY(-2px), no glow.

rules.name: The Recess Rule
rules.body: 'Inside' and 'selected' go darker (to Ink Black), not lighter. Elevation in this system points down.

dos: Do keep chrome monochrome and spend colour on data. Brass = live control; green/amber/red = booking status; the eight bright hues = hiking days.
Do use 2px corners for everything rectangular. Reserve 50% for genuinely circular objects and 8px only for something floating free of the layout.
Do separate with a 1px --border hairline and a tonal step. That is the whole depth system.
Do put the active-state edge bar on the right (leading) edge, and keep it 2-3px.
Do write region, field and unit labels at 10-11px, weight 600, 0.1em tracking, Stone Muted.
Do keep transitions at .15s on colour and border only, and .25s for drawers and the toast.
Do use pure #fff and real shadows on marks drawn over the satellite map — that is where the palette legitimately inverts.
Do make responsive changes structural (column becomes horizontal scroller, sidebar becomes drawer) and bump specific font sizes explicitly at 768px.
Do keep form inputs at 16px on mobile so iOS does not zoom on focus.
donts: Don't add a box-shadow to anything that is not physically above the map or the app shell. No card shadows, no hover lift, no glow.
Don't make 'selected' lighter. Selected and inset go darker, to Ink Black.
Don't introduce a webfont or a display face. One system stack, differentiated by weight and tracking.
Don't use clamp() or viewport-relative type. The ladder is fixed and hand-tuned.
Don't use brass for decoration, large fills, or inactive states. If it is not the live control, it is grey.
Don't introduce a second radius, a second divider mechanism, or a fourth surface tone.
Don't add icons to navigation. This system is label-only, and its labels are its character.
Don't apply letter-spacing or text-transform: uppercase to Hebrew body copy.
Don't put a saturated status colour on screen without its 12%-alpha wash behind it.
Don't reach for a modal. The existing system has none: it uses panel switching, inline drawers, inline forms and native confirm() for destruction.
